transcript.text: micrwave keeps tripping the eletric, not every time but like 1 in 3 when i press start, whole kitchen goes off. had to reset the fuse box 4 times today

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Because your microwave is tripping the main electricity supply when you press start, this indicates a serious internal fault—most likely a short circuit in the high-voltage components (such as the capacitor, diode, or magnetron) or a door interlock switch failure. This is not something that can be safely diagnosed or repaired by an owner. Please stop using the microwave immediately and do not attempt to reset the fuse box repeatedly, as this poses a fire risk and can cause further damage. Do not open the casing yourself; high-voltage capacitors inside microwaves can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged. You need to have a qualified appliance engineer inspect the unit. They will be able to safely test the internal components and determine if it is repairable or if replacement is necessary.

candidates: Internal short circuit (e.g., high-voltage capacitor, diode, magnetron, or door interlock switch) (high)
Faulty mains lead or internal power supply fault (medium)

reading.symptom: keeps tripping the electric when pressing start

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "keeps tripping the electric when pressing start". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (repeated reset): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
